P001.text: Act on the ordered deployment revisions spanning the suspected onset of unusually slow exports.

P002.text: The target property is an elevated probability of exceeding one hour under comparable workloads, rather than a change in median duration.

P003.text: The packet supplies neither a verified earlier good revision nor a reproducibly bad later revision; establishing these endpoints is a prerequisite.

P004.text: Before testing, define the reference workload mix, acceptable tail rate, material increase, confidence criteria and sample budget.

P005.text: Assume representative exports can be tested safely on isolated workers using authorized snapshots or scheduled overnight workloads; verify that assumption.

P006.text: Record worker revision, configuration, dependencies, workspace size, object count and concurrency so changes outside revision history are not silently attributed to code.

P007.text: First repeat tests of candidate earlier and later revisions under matched conditions to establish good and bad endpoints.

P008.text: Use consistent queue-entry-to-upload-completion timing across revisions; validate timing comparability because trace coverage differs.

P009.text: Run only isolated, resource-capped tests or approved overnight trials, without requesting customer reruns during business hours.

P010.text: Stop tests if they threaten scheduled exports, exceed resource limits or exhaust the agreed budget.

P011.text: Once endpoints are established, test a midpoint revision on repeated representative exports.

P012.text: If confidently good, replace the good endpoint with that midpoint; if confidently bad, replace the bad endpoint.

P013.text: Repeat, discarding only the history incompatible with the classification under the single-transition assumption.

P014.text: For inconclusive results, collect additional trials within budget; never discard history from a single fast export or treat a build failure as a performance result.

P015.text: Stop at adjacent confidently classified revisions, or retain an unresolved interval when further classification is infeasible.

P016.text: For each revision, observe the number of exports tested, the fraction exceeding one hour and its uncertainty, with workload and load recorded.

P017.text: Classify good only when the prespecified evidence supports the acceptable range, and bad only when it supports the defined elevated range; otherwise classify inconclusive.

P018.text: Choose the replication and repeated-testing rule in advance so repeated midpoint decisions do not accumulate uncontrolled error.

P019.text: An export still running after one hour has crossed the threshold; a test stopped earlier has an unknown threshold outcome and must not count as fast.

P020.text: Where comparable trace spans exist, separate queue wait, worker execution, object reads and upload time to identify where additional time accumulates.

P021.text: Missing spans indicate missing evidence, not zero delay.

P022.text: Each decisive midpoint result shrinks the candidate transition interval.

P023.text: Conditional on valid endpoints, comparable trials and a persistent single transition, repeated elimination localizes the first revision associated with the defined tail-rate increase to the final boundary.

P024.text: It does not yet establish a sole cause.

P025.text: Retest both sides of that boundary on matched workloads and, if feasible, test a targeted revert or fix while holding other factors constant.

P026.text: If the regression and its reversal reproduce, choose a bounded overnight canary of the compatible revert or fix, with predefined tail-rate, failure and resource stop thresholds; expand only after adequate evidence, otherwise halt or roll back the canary.

P027.text: If endpoints or measurements cannot be established, choose a bounded deployment of consistent timing instrumentation, validate its overhead and gather evidence before attributing the delays or selecting a code rollback.

P028.text: Rare delays require enough trials: absence of a slow export in a small sample cannot establish goodness.

P029.text: Changing workspace mix, storage or network conditions, queue pressure, configuration and dependencies can confound revision comparisons; isolated replay may omit production interactions.

P030.text: Unequal trace coverage can create apparent phase differences.

P031.text: Flakiness, unbuildable revisions, several regressions, later fixes and interactions can invalidate binary elimination or leave several candidate boundaries.

P032.text: If results contradict a single transition, stop discarding halves and test smaller intervals or separate suspected factors.

P033.text: Report gaps and inconclusive endpoints explicitly.

P034.text: A localized boundary supports association under tested conditions; production causality and deployment safety require confirmation and monitored rollout.
